question: If two points on a line lie in a plane, what follows?
solution: Under the usual reading that “two points” means two distinct points, apply the basic line-plane incidence fact: if two distinct points of a line lie in a plane, the entire line lies in that plane. Therefore the answer is D.

answerCheck.derivedAnswer: D under the usual reading of two distinct points
answerCheck.reason: The line-plane incidence axiom makes every point of the line a point of the plane once two distinct points are shared. A single shared point would not suffice: the z-axis and plane z=0 share only the origin. The ordinary school phrase two points is understood as distinct here; the proposed node makes that condition explicit.

Other plane axioms are siblings, while line-plane classification helps apply the target distinction between containment and a single intersection.
